results.title: Brain region identification
results.question: What are the major subdivisions of the Drosophila mushroom body?
results.response: The major subdivisions of the Drosophila [mushroom body](https://www.virtualflybrain.org/reports/FBbt_00005801 "Open mushroom body in Virtual Fly Brain") are the calyx, pedunculus, and mushroom body lobe system. This information comes from the VFB database. VFB records show that the mushroom body is divided into these three parts: the calyx, which receives sensory interneuron afferents; the pedunculus, a thick axon bundle extending from the calyx to the base of the lobes; and the mushroom body lobe system, which consists of a vertical branch and a medial branch. VFB holds various data related to the mushroom body, including [602](https://v2.virtualflybrain.org/org.geppetto.frontend/geppetto?q=FBbt_00005801,NeuronsPartHere "Run in VFB: Neurons with some part in mushroom body") records of neurons with some part in the mushroom body, [176](https://v2.virtualflybrain.org/org.geppetto.frontend/geppetto?q=FBbt_00005801,PartsOf "Run in VFB: Parts of mushroom body") records of parts of the mushroom body, and [2](https://v2.virtualflybrain.org/org.geppetto.frontend/geppetto?q=FBbt_00005801,SubclassesOf "Run in VFB: Subclasses of mushroom body") records of subclasses of the mushroom body. For further information, the user can explore these records and the [22,137](https://v2.virtualflybrain.org/org.geppetto.frontend/geppetto?q=FBbt_00005801,ImagesNeurons "Run in VFB: Images of neurons with some part in mushroom body") images of neurons with some part in the mushroom body available in VFB.

results.title: Neuron characterisation
results.question: What is known about the LPLC2 visual neuron type? Where is it, what does it connect to, and what is its function?
results.response: The [LPLC2](https://www.virtualflybrain.org/reports/VFB_jrch0fva "Open LPLC2 in Virtual Fly Brain") visual neuron type is a type of neuron in the fly brain. VFB records show that it has a cell body located in the dorsal area of the lateral cell body rind. The connectome data indicates that LPLC2 has a distinct dendritic arbor in each lobula plate layer, extending outwards from the main fiber in the direction of motion detection for the layer, allowing it to detect looming stimuli. In the lobula, its main dendritic arbors are in layers 4 and 5B, with minor processes in layer 5A, and presynaptic sites in layer 4. VFB holds data on its projections, which show that it projects to an optic glomerulus of the PVLP, anterior to LPLC1 and dorsal to LC4. The activity of LPLC2 elicits a jump escape response. VFB has annotated approximately 80 of these cells per optic lobe and records show that they are cholinergic. VFB does not currently hold comprehensive data on all of its connections, but the available data indicate that its arbors span approximately 25 lobula optic columns, overlapping with other LPLC2 cells.

results.question: Trace a pathway from olfactory receptor neurons to the lateral horn. What are the intermediate neuron types and their connections?

A high-level pathway from olfactory receptor neurons to lateral horn is olfactory receptor neurons -> antennal lobe projection neuron -> [adult lateral horn](https://www.virtualflybrain.org/reports/FBbt_00007053 "Open adult lateral horn in Virtual Fly Brain"). 

VFB holds a significant amount of data related to the adult lateral horn, including images, neurons with various types of terminals in this region, tracts/nerves innervating it, lineage clones found in it, images of neurons with parts in it, and transgene expression data. Additionally, examining the images and transgene expression data in the adult lateral horn may provide more insights into the organization and function of this pathway.

results.question: Give me a comprehensive profile of the giant fiber neuron: its anatomy, connectivity, available driver lines, and relevant publications.
results.response:
The [giant fiber neuron](https://www.virtualflybrain.org/reports/FBbt_00004020 "Open giant fiber neuron in Virtual Fly Brain"), also known as DNp01, is a large adult descending neuron that controls jump escape behavior, as described by Thomas and Wyman (1984). VFB records show that this neuron has specific anatomy and connectivity. The connectome data indicates that the giant fiber neuron has axo-axonic synapses on descending neurons. 

VFB holds data on the genetic tools and expression patterns associated with the giant fiber neuron, including split-GAL4 and intersectional lines. VFB has annotated 10 genetic tool/expression pattern rows for the giant fiber neuron. 

For more information on the giant fiber neuron, including its anatomy, connectivity, and relevant publications, the user can query VFB using the neuron's name. VFB does not currently hold a comprehensive list of all publications related to the giant fiber neuron, but the user can search for relevant papers, such as those by Thomas and Wyman (1984), to learn more about this neuron's function and properties.
